title: The Sub 37: the Sub Phatty grown into a two-note synth with a sequencer
intro: Moog Music’s Phatty line began in 2006 with the Little Phatty, the last instrument Bob Moog worked on, a programmable two-oscillator mono synth with the ladder filter. The Sub Phatty of 2013 added a sub oscillator, a feedback channel and MultiDrive in a smaller, knob-per-function box. The Sub 37, released in 2014, develops the Sub Phatty: duo mode for two notes, a second mod bus, looping envelopes with delay and hold, an arpeggiator and a 64-step sequencer, 256 presets and 37 keys. The first edition, the Tribute Edition, carries Bob Moog’s signature.

timeline.name: Moog Little Phatty
timeline.text: A programmable two-oscillator mono synth with the ladder filter and 37 keys, the last instrument Bob Moog worked on; its first edition was the Tribute Edition.

timeline.name: Moog Sub Phatty
timeline.text: Two oscillators, a sub oscillator, noise and a feedback channel into the ladder filter with MultiDrive, and two envelopes, on a 25-key keyboard with a control for most functions.

timeline.name: Moog Sub 37 Tribute Edition
timeline.text: The Sub Phatty’s voice with duo mode, two mod buses, looping DAHDSR envelopes, a filter slope of 6 to 24 dB, an arpeggiator and 64-step sequencer, 256 presets and 37 keys with aftertouch.

timeline.name: Moog Subsequent 37
timeline.text: The Sub 37’s successor, with a reworked mixer and more headroom, and a few panel changes.

relatives.name: Minimoog Model D
relatives.text: The first Moog with a keyboard, mixer and ladder filter in one portable case. Players patched its output back into its external input to fatten it, the trick the Sub 37’s FDBK/EXT IN channel builds in.

relatives.name: Minimoog Voyager
relatives.text: Moog’s programmable return to the Minimoog’s design, with presets and a touch surface: an older, larger relative of the Sub 37.

relatives.name: Moog Sub 25
relatives.text: A smaller sibling on the same engine, with 25 keys, duo mode and a latching arpeggiator but one mod bus and fewer knobs.
